cumleler: Do two people with nearly identical audiograms understand speech in noise equally?
In this example, two patients have nearly identical audiograms and quiet scores.
Patient A's SNR loss is two decibels; near normal in noise.
Patient B's SNR loss is twelve decibels; moderate difficulty in noise.
Even with the same hearing aid, their experience in noise will differ.
A speech-in-noise test makes this difference measurable.
